dimension: Tracer -> CNC geometry handoff
title: Line-art contour selection is applied to text and SVG geometry, not just traced line art
claim: ADR-218's contour selection is geometric, not source-scoped, so it also removes the outer contour of text glyphs and imported SVG rings whose wall is under the layer bit — silently, since findDroppedCncLayers only reports fully empty layers. For a real end mill this matches ADR-218's documented criterion. The defect is the threshold's use of CncTool.diameterMm for V/engraving bits (eng-15 is 3.175 mm shank, machine.ts:259-263), which makes an engrave layer discard glyph/SVG outlines that the actual sub-millimetre groove would cut correctly.
referenceBehavior: Easel, VCarve and Carbide Create all engrave both the outer contour and the counter of every glyph; there is no bit-diameter-dependent contour suppression in any of them. ADR-218's own Context (DECISIONS.md 9354-9364) scopes the problem exclusively to 'a boundary trace (the Line Art preset)' vectorizing 'a stroked drawing', and its field repro is job111.gcode from a traced image — nothing in the ADR contemplates vector text or SVG input.
suggestedFix: Scope the selection to geometry that actually came from a boundary trace. collectLayerContours already switches on object.kind (collect-cnc-contours.ts:32-38), so carry a per-contour `fromTrace` flag on CollectedCncContour (set only for 'traced-image' objects, optionally only when traceMode is 'filled-contours') and have lineArtContoursForLayer pass only those polylines to selectLineArtContours, splicing the untouched rest back in. This narrows an existing deletion to the case the ADR describes; it introduces no gate, block, or prompt.
verifierReasoning: The mechanical claim is accurate and I re-walked it. compile-cnc-job.ts:227 calls lineArtContoursForLayer on the layer's whole polyline set; :276-287 gates only on lineArtSelectionApplies(settings.cutType) and never inspects object kind; the polylines come from compile-cnc-job.ts:68-69 -> collect-cnc-contours.ts:25-47, whose switch treats 'imported-svg', 'text', 'traced-image' and 'shape' identically (no kind or traceMode is carried onto CollectedCncContour). lineArtSelectionApplies('engrave') is true (line-art-contours.ts:41-48). So yes: a glyph's outer bowl and its counter are a directly-contained ring pair and, when the four bbox gaps are <= the layer bit, line-art-contours.ts:66 drops the OUTER contour with no output that mentions it (findDroppedCncLayers, compile-cnc-diagnostics.ts:16-33, only reports layers that produce zero toolpaths, so a partial drop is invisible). Where the finding overreaches: ADR-218's Decision is written purely geometrically ('a pair qualifies only under direct containment with per-side bounding-box gaps at or below the layer's bit diameter'), with no scoping to traced objects, and its Consequences say 'existing projects whose artwork contains sub-bit-diameter double lines change output on their next compile ... That is the point'. For a real end mill the glyph case IS the ADR's case: the two edges of an 'O' bowl thinner than the bit are exactly a double-line whose second pass re-cuts destroyed material, so 'inner' is defensible and 'both' restores the old output per layer. I also did not measure Roboto's stem width anywhere in this tree — the '0.6-0.9 mm at 10 mm type' figure is the author's estimate, not verified code or fixture output, and I did not run any compile to observe a dropped glyph contour. The residue that is a real defect is narrower: CncTool.diameterMm for V/engraving bits is the shank, not the cutting width (machine.ts:254-263: vb-30 3.175, vb-90 12.7, eng-15 diameterMm 3.175 with tipAngleDeg 15), so an 'engrave' layer using eng-15 — which cuts a groove a few tenths wide — has its glyph/SVG outer contours judged un-machinable at 3.175 mm and dropped, losing letter outlines on a cut that would have been fine. That is a wrong computed value, not a scoping bug, and the honest remedy is either using an effective cutting width for the threshold or a Job Review line naming the contours the selection removed (never a refusal).

dimension: Tracer -> CNC geometry handoff
title: Comments claim traced curves survive to compile; the shipped presets hand CNC a line-only sample
claim: Two comments are materially stale for the three shipped filled presets: ImportImageDialog.tsx:298-301 ('Curves stay at imagetracerjs's analytic fidelity through to compile') and scene-object.ts:191-193 ('pre-traced (via imagetracerjs + parseSvg)') — the Line Art/Smooth/Sharp lane runs the in-house contour backend (ADR-123), resamples its fitted cubics at cubic-fit.ts:325/30, and hands CNC line-only curve subpaths, so DEFAULT_MACHINE_CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM is an identity round-trip on traced geometry. The trace-to-paths.ts:1-6 quadratic-to-cubic sentence is NOT stale; it correctly describes the imagetracerjs multi-colour lane it heads and only needs a lane qualifier.
evidence:
The claims. src/ui/trace/ImportImageDialog.tsx:298-301: 'Direct tracedata path: ColoredPath[] directly, skipping the SVG-string + parseSvg detour that flattened Beziers at coarse tolerance. Curves stay at imagetracerjs's analytic fidelity through to compile.' src/core/trace/trace-to-paths.ts:4-6: 'Quadratic segments are converted exactly to canonical cubics.' trace-to-paths.ts:134-135: 'no parseSvg step in between, so curve fidelity survives.' src/core/scene/scene-object.ts:191-192 also says TracedImage is 'pre-traced (via imagetracerjs + parseSvg)'.

What actually runs. Line Art / Smooth / Sharp all satisfy isBinaryContourPreset (contour-trace.ts:48-52: not centerline/edge, numberOfColors===2, fixedPalette.length===2), so trace-to-paths.ts:181 dispatches to traceImageToContourColoredPaths and imagetracerjs is never loaded. That backend fits real cubics at contour-trace.ts:319 `const cubics = fitCubicsThroughPoints(...)` and then immediately throws them away at line 325 `const sampled = sampleCubics(cubics, true);` — sampleCubics (src/core/geometry/cubic-fit.ts:62-73) returns Vec2[] only, at SAMPLE_STEP_PX = 1.5 px per sample (cubic-fit.ts:30). finishLoop returns a Polyline. contour-trace.ts:141-143 then wraps it: `withCanonicalTraceCurves([{ color: CONTOUR_COLOR, polylines }])` — the object has no `curves` key, so trace-curves.ts:6 fills it with `path.polylines.map(polylineToCurveSubpath)`, and polylineToCurveSubpath (src/core/scene/curve-path.ts:101-108) builds `segments: polyline.points.slice(1).map((to) => ({ kind: 'line' as const, to }))`. Every segment is a line.

Consequence at the CNC boundary: collect-cnc-contours.ts:57-61 calls flattenColoredPathCurves with toleranceMm DEFAULT_MACHINE_CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM (0.025, curve-path.ts:12), which for line-only subpaths is an identity round-trip (flattenSegment on a 'line' just emits `to`). So the machine tolerance knob has no effect on traced geometry: chord error is fixed by the tracer's 1.5 px sampling, not by the compiler. At the default 254 DPI bitmap import (0.1 mm/px, src/ui/common/image-import.ts:8 and 44-46) that is ~0.075-0.15 mm per G1 block. This CONFIRMS the prior audit's 'the tracer discards its cubics; CNC cuts a dense polyline sample'. I computed the resulting chord sagitta (s^2/8R: 1.5 px on a 100 px radius is 0.0003 mm) and it is not a fidelity problem — the defect here is the false documentation, which would lead the next reader to tune DEFAULT_MACHINE_CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM expecting it to affect traced parts.
referenceBehavior: Not a reference-tool divergence — this is a code-vs-comment divergence. The authoritative statement in the tree is contour-trace.ts:311-312 ('the measured-loop output tail: G1 cubic fit ... resampled to the polyline contract') and ADR-123's adoption of the in-house contour backend, both of which contradict the imagetracerjs comments left behind at the dialog and trace-to-paths headers.
suggestedFix: Correct the three stale comments to describe the backend that actually runs: at ImportImageDialog.tsx:298-301 say the geometry is returned as ColoredPath[] in source-pixel coordinates from the in-house contour backend (ADR-123) with cubics already resampled to the polyline contract; at trace-to-paths.ts:4-6 and 134-135 scope the quadratic-to-cubic sentence to the imagetracerjs multi-colour lane; at scene-object.ts:191-192 drop the 'via imagetracerjs + parseSvg' clause. No code change.
verifierReasoning: I re-walked the whole chain and it holds. TRACE_PRESETS (src/core/trace/trace-presets.ts:13) has 'Line Art' (line 14), 'Centerline' (:57, traceMode 'centerline'), the edge preset (traceMode 'edge' at :90), 'Smooth' (:119) and 'Sharp' (:153); Line Art/Smooth/Sharp all carry numberOfColors: 2 with a 2-entry fixedPalette and no traceMode, so isBinaryContourPreset (contour-trace.ts:48-52) is true and trace-to-paths.ts:181 returns traceImageToContourColoredPaths before loadTracer() is ever reached — imagetracerjs is not in that lane. contour-trace.ts:319 fits cubics, :325 immediately calls sampleCubics, which returns Vec2[] (cubic-fit.ts:62-73, re-exported through trace/fit-cubics.ts:3) at SAMPLE_STEP_PX = 1.5 (cubic-fit.ts:30). contour-trace.ts:141-143 wraps the result with withCanonicalTraceCurves, and trace-curves.ts:6 fills the missing `curves` from path.polylines.map(polylineToCurveSubpath), which builds only { kind: 'line' } segments (curve-path.ts:101-108). collect-cnc-contours.ts:57-60 then flattens at DEFAULT_MACHINE_CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM (curve-path.ts:12, 0.025) — an identity round-trip on line-only subpaths. So 'Curves stay at imagetracerjs's analytic fidelity through to compile' (ImportImageDialog.tsx:298-301) and 'pre-traced (via imagetracerjs + parseSvg)' (scene-object.ts:191-193) are both materially false for all three shipped filled presets. Where the finding overreaches: the third comment, trace-to-paths.ts:1-6 ('Quadratic segments are converted exactly to canonical cubics'), describes tracedataToColoredPaths, which is still the live conversion for the multi-colour no-fixed-palette lane reached at trace-to-paths.ts:182-185 — that sentence is accurate for the code it heads, merely unqualified about which lane runs. The :134-135 'no parseSvg step in between' is also literally true (parseSvg is not called on either lane). This is documentation-only, no machine motion or setting is affected, and the author's own sagitta estimate shows no fidelity consequence — P3 stands.

dimension: Settings schema + shipped defaults
title: Climb and conventional are inverted: default "climb" emits conventional windings
claim: wantsCounterClockwise() maps climb to counter-clockwise for profile-outside and clockwise for profile-inside/pocket, which is the CONVENTIONAL direction for a right-hand (M3) cutter — so the shipped default cutDirection 'climb' emits conventional toolpaths, and an operator who selects "Conventional" gets actual climb.
referenceBehavior: For a right-hand / M3 (top-view clockwise) cutter, conventional milling is counter-clockwise around the OUTSIDE of a part and clockwise inside a cutout; climb is clockwise outside and counter-clockwise inside. RouterCIM's Cut Direction help states 'moving around a finished part counter-clockwise is considered conventional cutting while a clockwise part path is climb cutting' and 'For an outside profile, choose clockwise' (https://www.cimtechsoftware.com/RouterCIM_Online_Help/cutdirection.htm). The equivalent handheld-router rule is the same physics: 'conventional cutting would be cutting counterclockwise around the outside of a part and clockwise on the inside of a cutout' (https://www.woodwiki.org/guides/router-feed-direction). It also matches the standard cutter-compensation convention: G41 (comp LEFT of the programmed path, i.e. material on the RIGHT of travel) is climb for a right-hand cutter. DISCLOSURE OF CONFLICT: Vectric's own 2D Profile help page labels 'Climb (CCW)' for BOTH the Outside and Inside strategies (https://docs.vectric.com/docs/V10.0/VCarvePro/ENU/Help/form/uiProfileMachineForm/), which cannot be right for both sides and appears to be a copy-paste defect in their docs; ADR-251 may have been written from that page.
suggestedFix: Swap the two return expressions in wantsCounterClockwise (motion-polish.ts:80-81): profile-outside -> `direction === 'conventional'`, profile-inside/pocket -> `direction === 'climb'`. Then flip the assertion in compile-cnc-climb-default.test.ts:63 to expect clockwise, correct the material-side sentence in motion-polish.ts:7-11 and machine.ts:55, and amend ADR-251/ADR-252. Nothing is blocked or added — only the direction mapping changes. Verify on a physical coupon before merging: cut the same square with 'Climb' before and after and compare edge quality and chip direction.
verifierReasoning:
Citation is exact. src/core/cnc/motion-polish.ts:79-83 reads `if (cutType === 'profile-outside') return direction === 'climb';` / `if (cutType === 'profile-inside' || cutType === 'pocket') return direction === 'conventional';`, and motion-polish.ts:44-57 forces that winding on the dominant contour (mirroring holes, ADR-252). Frame is real CCW in top view: signedAreaMm2 is shoelace with 'positive = counter-clockwise' in the machine frame (src/core/geometry/polyline-orientation.ts:1-2,6-18) and contours pass through toMachineCoords (src/core/cnc/collect-cnc-contours.ts:73-76), whose header states the scene Y-down frame is flipped to a GRBL Y-up frame for front-* origins (src/core/devices/origin-transform.ts:5-13).

I re-derived the physics myself rather than accepting the finding's. Tool centre feeding +X, M3 = ω = -ω ẑ (CW viewed from above). Uncut chip thickness at tooth angle θ is h = f_z·cosθ (previous tooth cut the same angular position one feed-per-tooth back), so cutting only occurs on the leading half, θ ∈ (-90°,90°). With material on the LEFT (+Y), the engaged arc is θ ∈ [θ0, 90°); CW rotation means θ decreases, so a tooth enters at θ=90° with h=0 and leaves at θ0 with h=max — thin→thick = CONVENTIONAL (up-milling). Force check agrees: the tooth at the +Y contact moves +X, so the reaction on the tool is -X, opposing the feed (the router pushes back = controlled/conventional cut). Repeating with material on the RIGHT gives thick→thin and a reaction along the feed (self-feeding) = CLIMB. So with M3, climb needs material on the RIGHT of travel; walking a part's exterior with the part on the right is CLOCKWISE, and a hole with material on the right is COUNTER-CLOCKWISE. The code returns exactly the opposite in both cases. Independent cross-checks agree: G41 (comp left of path → material right of travel) is climb for a right-hand cutter, and the handheld-router rule (CCW around the outside is the safe, non-climb feed) implies climb-outside = CW.

End-to-end walk: DEFAULT_CNC_LAYER_SETTINGS.cutDirection = 'climb' (src/core/scene/machine.ts:316); a default profile-outside square compiles counter-clockwise, pinned by src/core/cnc/compile-cnc-climb-default.test.ts:63 `expect(isCounterClockwise(...)).toBe(true)` — i.e. conventional milling shipped under the label 'Climb'. The mirror case is the dangerous one: an operator who picks 'Conventional' in the layer dropdown (src/ui/layers/CncLayerToolFields.tsx:231) to avoid grabbing on a belt/backlash machine gets wantCcw=false = CW on an outside profile = actual climb, the exact self-feeding failure ADR-251 names as the risk it accepts.

Not documented-as-intended in a way that rescues it: the erroneous premise is asserted, not decided — motion-polish.ts:7-11, machine.ts:54-55, DECISIONS.md ADR-251 (line 11646-11648, 'outside-profile = counter-clockwise with an M3 / top-view-clockwise spindle') and ADR-252 (line 11696-11697, 'with an M3 spindle climb keeps the material on the LEFT of travel'). The ADRs' *intent* (default to climb for a cleaner kept edge) is not achieved by the code, so this is a bug the ADRs must be amended for, not an accepted trade-off. The fix adds no guard — it swaps two return expressions, flips the pinned assertion, and corrects three comments plus two ADRs. Caution for whoever lands it: ADR-250 lead sides are derived from winding relative to the dominant sign (src/core/cnc/profile-lead-passes.ts:53-60, 95-110), so re-verify lead placement and the ADR-252 hole mirror after the swap, and cut a physical coupon before merging — nothing in the suite measures the actual chip direction.

dimension: Settings schema + shipped defaults
title: Default spindleRpm equals default spindleMaxRpm; lowering the ceiling refuses Start on every layer
claim: The layer-spindle-vs-ceiling arm of runCncPreflight (src/core/preflight/cnc-preflight.ts:137-144) is a policy refusal, not compile integrity: compile-cnc-job.ts:166 already clamps via capSpindle (src/core/cnc/compile-cnc-helpers.ts:46-49, `Math.min(spindleRpm, spindleMaxRpm)`), so the program factually CAN be produced and can never emit an out-of-range S. It should be a Job Review warning ('layer requests 12000 RPM, ceiling is 10000 — the job runs at 10000') instead of blocking Start. Scope is narrower than claimed: it only bites layers with NO feedSource (hand-tuned layers, or a layer with `cnc` undefined); auto-provenance layers self-heal on the same edit. The 'default equals the ceiling' framing is not itself a defect.
evidence:
Defaults: src/core/scene/machine.ts:288 `spindleMaxRpm: 12000` and machine.ts:307 `spindleRpm: 12000` — equal, so any downward edit of the ceiling immediately puts every untouched layer above it.

The compiler already resolves this safely — src/core/cnc/compile-cnc-job.ts:166:
```
spindleRpm: capSpindle(settings.spindleRpm, config.params.spindleMaxRpm),
```
and src/core/cnc/compile-cnc-helpers.ts:46-49 returns `Math.min(spindleRpm, spindleMaxRpm)`. The emitted `M3 S<rpm>` can therefore never exceed the ceiling.

Despite that, src/core/preflight/cnc-preflight.ts:137-144 still raises a hard issue:
```
if (!(settings.spindleRpm > 0) || settings.spindleRpm > config.params.spindleMaxRpm) {
  issues.push({ code: 'cnc-settings-invalid', message: ... });
}
```
and src/ui/laser/start-job-readiness.ts:392 turns a non-ok preflight into `{ ok: false }` for Start.

Walk-through: operator opens a default CNC project (three layers, each spindleRpm 12000), then sets Spindle max to 10000 in Material & Bit (src/ui/machine/CncSetupPanel.tsx:181-190). updateCncMachine (src/ui/state/machine-actions.ts, updateCncMachine) patches only params — it never re-clamps layer.cnc.spindleRpm. Every layer now reports 'spindle 12000 RPM is outside (0, 10000]' and Start is refused, even though the program that would be emitted is a perfectly valid S10000. The operator must hand-edit each layer's Spindle field to recover.
referenceBehavior: CLAUDE.md rule 7 permits only transport preconditions, compile integrity, and handoff consistency as refusals. This is none of them: the program factually CAN be produced and is already clamped to a legal S value, so the refusal is a policy judgment and belongs in the Job Review warnings list. Easel and Carbide Create clamp the requested RPM into the machine's range and post the job rather than refusing to generate G-code.
suggestedFix: Delete the spindle-ceiling arm of the check in cnc-preflight.ts:137 (keep only the `!(spindleRpm > 0)` compile-integrity half) and surface 'layer requests 12000 RPM, machine ceiling is 10000 — the job will run at 10000' as a Job Review warning. This REMOVES a refusal, which is normal work. Optionally also lower DEFAULT_CNC_LAYER_SETTINGS.spindleRpm below spindleMaxRpm so the shipped pair is not on the boundary.
verifierReasoning:
Citations check out: cnc-preflight.ts:137-144 raises 'cnc-settings-invalid' when `settings.spindleRpm > config.params.spindleMaxRpm`; compile-cnc-job.ts:166 calls capSpindle; compile-cnc-helpers.ts:46-49 returns Math.min. The Start path is real — src/io/gcode/prepare-output.ts:40-49 makes `ok:false` carry the PreflightResult, and src/ui/laser/start-job-readiness.ts:391-393 turns that into `{ok:false, messages}`. So the refusal is genuine and is not one of the three permitted categories (transport / compile integrity / handoff consistency); removing it is legitimate work under rule 7.

But the finding's mechanism claim is partly wrong. It states 'updateCncMachine patches only params — it never re-clamps layer.cnc.spindleRpm'. src/ui/state/machine-actions.ts:130 calls refreshAutomaticCncFeeds on every updateCncMachine, and for material-recipe layers materialSpindleRpm takes `lesserPositive([input.spindleRpm, input.machineSpindleMaxRpm, ...])` (src/core/cnc/machine-starters/resolve-cnc-auto-settings.ts:131-142), while starter layers get an explicit spindleRpm cap keyed to machine.params.spindleMaxRpm (src/core/cnc/resolve-cnc-machine-starter.ts:101-105). Those layers are re-clamped the instant the ceiling drops and never trip the check. Only layers with feedSource absent (refreshAutomaticCncLayer returns early at src/ui/state/cnc-auto-seeding.ts:64-66) keep the stale RPM. 'No in-place fix' is also overstated: the message names the layer, and the layer's Spindle field is bounded by `max={spindleMaxRpm}` with a clamping parse (src/ui/layers/CncLayerAdvancedFields.tsx:117-127 and src/ui/layers/CncLayerPrimitives.tsx:33-37), so a single edit clears it. Severity downgraded to P3: no wrong motion, no wrong cut, no silent setting loss — a superfluous refusal on a subset of layers.

title: profileLead is shipped default-on but has no UI anywhere — arc/radius/sweep and the opt-out are unreachable
claim: CncProfileLeadSettings is a compiled, persisted, default-ON setting that changes every closed profile pass, yet no UI writes or reads it — the operator cannot change the lead shape, radius, or sweep, and cannot opt out with shape:'none' except by hand-editing the .lf2.

Declared at src/core/scene/machine.ts:178 (`readonly profileLead?: CncProfileLeadSettings;`) and machine.ts:97-103. It is default-ON: src/core/cnc/profile-lead-passes.ts:72-82 resolves an absent field to `{ shape: 'arc', radiusMm: toolDiameterMm / 2 }`, and applyProfileLeadPasses (compile-cnc-job.ts:119-124) converts every closed profile-outside/inside contour pass into a led path3d pass. title: Pocket ring ladder can leave an uncut core when stepover exceeds 50% of diameter
claim: pocketToolpathRings stops as soon as the next inward offset collapses to nothing, with no final centre ring, so when stepMm exceeds the tool radius the innermost ring's tool sweep does not reach the pocket centre and a pillar of full-depth material is left standing.
evidence: pocket-paths.ts:41-46: `for (let k = 0; k < MAX_POCKET_RINGS; k += 1) { const inset = radius + k * stepMm; const ring = offsetClosedPolylinesForKerf(contours, -inset); if (ring.length === 0) break; rings.push(ring); }`. stepMm = (stepover/100) * toolDiameterMm (pocket-paths.ts:38) and clampStepoverPercent allows up to MAX_STEPOVER_PERCENT = 85 (pocket-paths.ts:21, 57-60); the UI exposes exactly that range — src/ui/layers/CncLayerAdvancedFields.tsx:174-176 `min={10} max={85} step={5}`. Walk-through: 6.35 mm end mill (radius 3.175), stepoverPercent 85 → stepMm 5.3975. Circular pocket of radius R = 8.175 mm. k=0: inset 3.175 → ring of radius 5.0, non-empty. k=1: inset 8.5725 > 8.175 → offset collapses, loop breaks. The single ring at radius 5.0 sweeps the annulus [5.0-3.175, 5.0+3.175] = [1.825, 8.175]. Everything inside radius 1.825 mm — a 3.65 mm diameter pillar at FULL pocket depth — is never touched. Generally, the last ring radius rho satisfies 0 < rho <= stepMm, and residue exists whenever rho > radius, i.e. whenever stepover > 50%. No test covers this: pocket-paths.test.ts only exercises stepover 40 (lines 26, 31, 42, 82) where stepMm < radius and the ladder does clear fully.
referenceBehavior: Vectric VCarve's Offset pocket strategy and Fusion 360's 2D Pocket both continue the offset ladder to the region's medial axis and add a final clean-up pass so no island of stock survives the roughing ladder regardless of the stepover chosen; leaving an uncut core is not an accepted outcome in either.
suggestedFix: After the loop breaks, emit one extra innermost ring at the collapse point — e.g. re-offset the last surviving ring inward by min(stepMm, its own inscribed radius) or, more simply, bisect between the last successful inset and the first failing one until the offset is non-empty and append that ring before the reversal at pocket-paths.ts:49-53. Do not clamp or refuse the operator's stepover.
verifierReasoning: pocket-paths.ts:40-46 is exactly the quoted loop, with `if (ring.length === 0) break;` and no terminal centre ring before the innermost-first reversal at :48-54. stepMm = (stepover/100)*toolDiameterMm (:38) and clampStepoverPercent caps at MAX_STEPOVER_PERCENT = 85 (:21,:57-60), matching the UI's `min={10} max={85}` (CncLayerAdvancedFields.tsx:174-176). I re-derived the residue condition independently: for a circular pocket of radius R the last surviving ring has radius rho = R - radius - k*step with rho in (0, step], and the tool sweeps inward only to rho - radius, so an uncut core of radius rho - radius survives whenever rho > radius — possible exactly when step > radius, i.e. stepover > 50%. Their 6.35 mm / 85% / R=8.175 mm arithmetic checks out (single ring at rho=5.0, 1.825 mm uncut core at full depth). No mitigation downstream: pocketToolpathsForSettings (cnc-rest-operation.ts:59-74) routes the default (absent) pocketStrategy straight to pocketToolpathRings with no clean-up pass. Severity stays P3 as filed rather than P2 because it requires the operator to raise stepover past 50% — DEFAULT_CNC_LAYER_SETTINGS.stepoverPercent is 40 (machine.ts:308), where the ladder does clear fully. The proposed fix (append one more innermost ring) adds no guard; do NOT clamp the stepover, which would be a rule-7 violation.

title: Two-stage v-carve: clearance pocket ignores the v-bit cone-height cap the ladder applies

title: Arc radius tolerance is 25.4x GRBL's real limit and its comment misstates GRBL's units
claim: The comment at circular-arc.ts:20 (duplicated at parse-gcode-program.ts:22) misdescribes 0.127 mm as GRBL's ~0.005 in arc tolerance; GRBL's check is 0.005 mm AND 0.1% of radius, so the constant is far looser than the controller it claims to mirror. It has no effect on emitted G-code — no production code produces a CncArcPass, and prepareHelicalMotion validates with end === start, so the delta is exactly zero. The impact is confined to the imported-.nc preview path and to a future reader trusting the comment; CncArcPass/appendArcPass is dead code.

The same premise is duplicated at src/io/gcode/parse-gcode-program.ts:22-23 (`// GRBL validates R-form/IJ arcs to ~0.005 in; allow the same order.` / `const ARC_RADIUS_TOLERANCE_MM = 0.127;`). GRBL 1.1 (gcode.c, centre-format offset mode) computes delta_r between the IJ-derived start radius and the target radius and fails with STATUS_GCODE_INVALID_TARGET (error:33) when delta_r > 0.005 AND delta_r > 0.001*r — those are millimetres, GRBL's internal unit. Failure walk-through: an arc with a 0.05 mm start/end radius mismatch on a 20 mm radius is judged 'ok' here and emitted natively as `G2 X… Y… I… J… F…` by cnc-grbl-strategy.ts:344-348; GRBL evaluates 0.05 > 0.005 and 0.05 > 0.02 and rejects the line with error:33, aborting the stream with the bit down in the cut. The real G2/G3 producer, prepareHelicalMotion (cnc-grbl-helical.ts:23), validates with `end: pass.start`, which makes start and end radii identical, so delta is exactly 0. The 0.127 value therefore only bites on the imported-.nc parser path today.
referenceBehavior: GRBL 1.1 rejects a centre-format arc whose start and end radii differ by more than 0.005 mm (and more than 0.1% of the radius) with error:33. Fusion/Vectric posts emit IJ to at least 4 decimals precisely to stay inside that window.
suggestedFix: Smallest correct change is the comment, not the value: replace 'Match the GRBL-order tolerance used by the external G-code parser: 0.005 in.' with a statement of what 0.127 mm actually is (an import-side leniency), in both circular-arc.ts:20 and parse-gcode-program.ts:22, so no future reader believes GRBL will accept what this accepts.
